title: Which command?
description: Match a TuxPixel task to the command that does it, when the other three do something else.

cards.prompt: Mira has lost track of where she is in the file tree and wants the full path of her current directory.
cards.why: `pwd` (print working directory) prints the absolute path of the directory you are in. `ls` lists its contents and `cd` moves you somewhere else.

cards.prompt: Jonas wants a new, empty directory called `levels`.
cards.why: `mkdir` makes directories. `touch` would create an empty file with that name, and `rmdir` removes a directory.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to delete the directory `old-art`, but only if it is empty, so nothing can be lost by accident.
cards.why: `rmdir` refuses to remove a directory that still holds files, which makes it the safe choice. `rm -r` would delete the contents as well.

cards.prompt: Jonas wants to rename `draft.txt` to `final.txt`, with no second copy left behind.
cards.why: `mv` moves and renames in one step. `cp` would leave `draft.txt` in place as well.

cards.prompt: Mira has to list every `.png` file below `~/projects` by looking through the directories, not through a prepared index.
cards.why: `find` walks a directory tree and tests each file name. `grep` searches inside files, not for file names, and `which` only looks for programs in `PATH`.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to see only the lines that contain `ERROR` in `build.log`.
cards.why: `grep` prints the lines of a file that match a pattern. `find` works on file names, and `sort` and `cut` do not search at all.

cards.prompt: Mira has a list of player names in `names.txt` and wants it in alphabetical order.
cards.why: `sort` orders lines. `uniq` only removes neighbouring duplicates, and it does not sort.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to know how many lines `notes.txt` has.
cards.why: `wc` counts, and `-l` makes it count lines. Without an option it prints lines, words and bytes.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to read a very long build log one screen at a time, scrolling both ways.
cards.why: `less` is a pager: space moves forward, `b` back, `q` quits. `cat` throws the whole file at the terminal and `tail` shows only the end.

cards.prompt: Jonas has `scores.csv` with comma-separated columns and wants only the third column.
cards.why: `cut` picks fields: `-d,` sets the comma as the separator and `-f3` selects the third field.

cards.prompt: Ada wants one `.tar.gz` file that bundles the directory `art/` with gzip compression.
cards.why: `tar -czf` creates (`c`) a gzip-compressed (`z`) archive in the file (`f`) you name. `-x` extracts instead of creating, and `gzip` and `bzip2` compress single files.

cards.prompt: Jonas wants a `.zip` archive of the directory `press/`, including everything inside it.
cards.why: `zip -r` builds a zip archive and walks into the directory. `unzip` unpacks one, and the `tar` command writes a different format.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to read the full manual page of `ls`.
cards.why: `man` opens the whole manual page. `whatis` shows only its one-line description, and `which` and `type` say where or what the command is.

cards.prompt: Ada needs a command that compresses files but cannot remember its name, only that it has to do with the word "compress". She searches the short descriptions of all manual pages.
cards.why: `apropos` (the same as `man -k`) searches the manual page descriptions for a word. `whatis` and `man` need the exact name of a command.

cards.prompt: Jonas wants just the one-line description of `tar`.
cards.why: `whatis` prints the short description from the manual page header. `which` prints a path and `type` says what kind of command it is.

cards.prompt: Ada has written `backup.sh` and wants to be able to start it with `./backup.sh`.
cards.why: `chmod +x` adds the execute permission. `chown` and `chgrp` change who owns the file but not what it may do.

cards.prompt: Mira wants the group `artists` to own the directory `art`, and nothing else about it to change.
cards.why: `chgrp` changes a file’s group. `groupadd` would create the group, and `chmod` takes permission bits, not group names.

cards.prompt: Mira wants `assets` in her home directory to be a shortcut that points to `/srv/assets`, with no copy of the data.
cards.why: `ln -s TARGET LINK` makes a symbolic link. `cp -r` would duplicate the data, and `mv` would take the directory away from `/srv`.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to see the user ID and all groups of the account `jonas`.
cards.why: `id` prints the UID, the primary group and the other groups of a user. `who` lists who is logged in, and `su` switches to that account.

cards.prompt: Mira, who is in the group `sudo`, wants to run a single command as root, using her own password.
cards.why: `sudo` runs one command with root rights after asking for your own password. `su` asks for the password of the account you switch to, which is root’s.

cards.prompt: Mira, as root, has to create an account for a new contractor and give it a home directory.
cards.why: `useradd -m` creates the user and the home directory, filled from `/etc/skel`. `passwd` only sets a password, and `groupadd` makes groups.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to see how much memory is free and how much is used.
cards.why: `free` reports memory (and swap), and `-h` makes the sizes readable. `df` is about disk space instead.

cards.prompt: Mira wants a live, constantly updating view of the processes that use the most CPU.
cards.why: `top` refreshes on its own. `ps` prints one snapshot and then returns to the prompt.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to read the messages that systemd has collected for the `ssh` service.
cards.why: `journalctl -u NAME` reads the journal for one service. `dmesg` shows the kernel’s messages, and `systemctl restart` would restart the service.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to know which IP address the name `build.tuxpixel.example` resolves to.
cards.why: `host` asks DNS and prints the address for a name. `ip addr show` lists the addresses of this machine’s own interfaces.
